title: Captain America: Brave New World
synopsis: Sam invites Isaiah Bradley to the White House. When Isaiah attacks the president and cannot remember doing it, Sam investigates.
verdictRationale: Sam protects the people at the reception and takes Isaiah’s account seriously. Knowing how his friend was treated in the past gives him reason to ask who took away Isaiah’s freedom to choose.
ageRationale: An apparent suicide occurs off camera. Burn injuries, bloody aftermaths and sustained combat make this a choice for older teens.
reflection: Betty visits Ross in prison after he gives up the presidency. Reconciliation begins with a daughter sitting beside her father while he answers for the harm he did.

title: Thunderbolts*
synopsis: Yelena crosses paths with other operatives sent into a trap and with Bob, a survivor of a secret experiment. The group must decide what they owe one another.
verdictRationale: Yelena remembers playing goalkeeper on a team that never won. What she loved was being there when someone made a mistake. Her decision to stay with Bob carries that childhood understanding of loyalty into the hardest encounter in the film.
ageRationale: A child is led to her death in a recurring memory. Other memories involve domestic abuse and addiction. The shadow consuming New York may distress viewers who identify with Bob’s despair.
reflection: Yelena knows how to finish a mission and hide what it costs her. Being present for Bob asks something different of her. She has to tell the truth about her own loneliness and allow others to stay with her, too.
